speaker: Doctor
text:
I understand you have fatigue, difficulty concentrating, and abnormal blood findings. To determine the specific cause, can you describe your symptoms in detail and how long you have been experiencing them?

REQUEST TEST: Complete Blood Count (CBC) with indices.
REQUEST TEST: Ferritin and Iron Studies.

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Complete Blood Count (CBC): Platelets 700,000 cells/m3 (thrombocytosis); Blood smear shows increased abnormal platelets. Iron Studies: Serum Iron decreased, Iron Saturation decreased, Serum Ferritin decreased, Total Iron Binding Capacity increased.

speaker: Doctor
text:
The abnormal blood count showing low iron alongside a significantly elevated platelet count (700,000) suggests this is not simple nutritional deficiency. Can you tell me if you have noticed any small red spots on your skin, easy bruising, or bleeding gums, which might indicate platelet dysfunction?

REQUEST IMAGES: Peripheral_Blood_Smear.

speaker: Patient
text: 53-year-old male. The patient has a 3-week history of fatigue, difficulty to concentrate, and dyspnea on exertion. He also experiences dizziness and digital pain that improves with cold. He has a long history of smoking.

speaker: Doctor
text:
The digital pain that improves with cold and your smoking history raise a strong suspicion for cold agglutinin disease. Can you confirm if your fingers, toes, or nose turn blue or white when exposed to the cold?

REQUEST TEST: Direct Antiglobulin Test (Coombs).
REQUEST TEST: Blood Smear for spherocytes and agglutination.
REQUEST IMAGES: Peripheral_Blood_Smear.

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Coombs Test: Negative. Blood Smear: Presence of agglutinated red blood cells in cold temperature portions of the smear; spherocytes not noted. Peripheral Blood Smear Image: Shows clumping of erythrocytes consistent with cold agglutination, particularly at the periphery of the slide; no spherocytes observed.

speaker: Doctor
text:
The presence of cold-induced agglutination on the smear, despite a negative Coombs test, confirms the mechanism is cold agglutinin mediated. Given your history of digital pain improving with cold and the elevated platelets, do you have a known infection with Mycoplasma pneumoniae or a history of lymphoma, which are common triggers for this condition?

REQUEST TEST: Cold Agglutinin Titer (at 4°C and 37°C).
REQUEST TEST: Lymphocyte Phenotyping (Flow Cytometry) and LDH level.

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Cold Agglutinin Titer: Positive at 4°C and 37°C; Lymphocyte Phenotyping: Abnormal B-cell population consistent with chronic lymphoproliferative disorder; LDH: Elevated.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Cold Agglutinin Disease secondary to Chronic Lymphoproliferative Disorder (likely Lymphoma).

The positive cold agglutinin titer, confirmed cold agglutination on the smear, and the elevated LDH combined with an abnormal B-cell population strongly indicate an underlying lymphoproliferative malignancy driving this autoimmune hemolytic process.
